listening:La Cellule Records.name: La Cellule Records
listening:La Cellule Records.teaser: The Var has no hi-fi listening bar; this Toulon record shop with a turntable to try records on is the nearest
listening:La Cellule Records.story: Be clear about this before you go: the Var has nothing like the Japanese-style listening bars, where a big valve system plays whole albums to a quiet room. What it has is this independent vinyl shop in central Toulon. Damien Lonegro opened it in 2014, and it keeps a listening deck so you can drop the needle on a record before you buy it. The bins run through rock, reggae, jazz and hip-hop, and the shop joins in Disquaire Day each spring. Come to dig, not to sit over a cocktail. There is no bar and no concert, just records, a turntable and someone happy to talk about them.
listening:La Cellule Records.why: Bring a want-list and ask Damien what has come in second-hand; the used bins are what turn up surprises.
facts: Central Toulon. Current listings give 5 rue Félix Pyat; older sources say rue Alézard, so check before you walk over (Oct 2026)
Records to browse and a turntable to try them on; no bar service and no live music
A weekday afternoon. Listings give Tuesday to Saturday, 10:00 to 19:00, closed Sunday and Monday, but they disagree, so check (Oct 2026)

listening:Oméga Live.name: Oméga Live
listening:Oméga Live.teaser: The small hall beside Toulon's Zénith, where the bands too big for a bar but too small for an arena play
listening:Oméga Live.story: Toulon's Zénith Oméga, on the boulevard Commandant Nicolas, has a big arena and, next to it, a much smaller hall called Oméga Live. It holds somewhere between two hundred and about seven hundred and fifty people, depending on whether the floor stands or sits, and it is the room where new acts and mid-sized tours play when they come through the Var. The bills run from rock and metal to electronic nights. Tandem, the Var's official contemporary-music organisation, puts on about sixty concerts a year across the department and runs Rade Side, Toulon's autumn music festival. Its listings at tandem83.com are the quickest way to see who is playing where.
listening:Oméga Live.why: Late autumn is when this room is busiest. Check the listings before you book a Toulon night.
facts: Zénith Oméga complex, boulevard Commandant Nicolas, central Toulon
Touring rock, metal, chanson and electronic acts through the autumn-to-spring season; check the Zénith and Tandem listings
Varies by show; buy through the venue or the usual French ticket sellers
Doors in the evening; arrive early for a place near the stage in a standing show

listening:Châteauvallon.name: Châteauvallon
listening:Châteauvallon.teaser: A summer amphitheatre for 1,167 people cut into the limestone above Ollioules, with a winter season indoors
listening:Châteauvallon.story: Châteauvallon sits in some 300 hectares of pine on the hills at Ollioules, a short drive west of Toulon. Since 2015 it and the Théâtre Liberté on Toulon's Place de la Liberté have shared one label as a scène nationale, a state-backed theatre. It programmes theatre, dance, music and jazz. The reason to cross the Var for it is the open-air amphitheatre, with 1,167 seats set into the rock, which is used only in June and July. The 2026 summer festival ran from 26 June to 28 July and opened with a new Madama Butterfly. It was the last festival programmed by the actor Charles Berling as director.
listening:Châteauvallon.why: In summer, book an amphitheatre night and come early to watch the light go off the pines before the show.
facts: Châteauvallon, Ollioules, about 15 minutes west of Toulon; the sister hall is the Théâtre Liberté in central Toulon
Theatre, dance and music; the indoor 2026-27 season is running now, and the open-air amphitheatre reopens for the June-July festival (2027 dates not yet seen, Oct 2026)

listening:Le Port des Créateurs.name: Le Port des Créateurs
listening:Le Port des Créateurs.teaser: An artist-run workshop on a small old-town square in Toulon, with free openings when the doors are thrown open
listening:Le Port des Créateurs.story: On the Place des Savonnières, in the lanes of Toulon's old town, an association founded in 2015 turned some 1,500 square metres into shared workshops: rooms for sound, image, publishing and visual art, where painters, musicians, designers and researchers use the same tools. It has worked as a tiers-lieu, a shared space for work and events, since 2016, and the culture ministry recognised it in 2021. Mostly it is a place of work: artists rent shared desks, and young cultural projects are coached here. A few times a year it opens up for exhibitions, concerts and parties, free to anyone. Lost in Châteaudouble, on 23 May 2026, was one.
listening:Le Port des Créateurs.why: Time a Toulon evening for one of its open nights and you see the city's young art scene in one room.
facts: Place des Savonnières, old town, Toulon
Exhibitions, concerts and open days a few times a year; check its own listings for the next one
Events free; professional membership EUR 80 a year for those who want to work there (Oct 2026)

around:Gorges du Verdon & Lac de Sainte-.name: Gorges du Verdon
around:Gorges du Verdon & Lac de Sainte-.teaser: Paddle out of a jade-green lake under 1970s floodwater and into the mouth of the canyon
around:Gorges du Verdon & Lac de Sainte-.story: The Verdon cuts a limestone canyon on the Var's northern edge; at the Dent d'Aire viewpoint the cliff stands about 700 metres above the river. The water's milky jade comes from fine mineral particles, fluorine and microalgae held in suspension. Where the gorge opens out, the river fills the Lac de Sainte-Croix, a reservoir EDF filled in 1973. The old village of Les Salles-sur-Verdon lies under it. Its last two residents were removed by gendarmes in January 1974, and its church was dynamited on 5 March 1974. With motorboats banned, you hear only paddles as you nose a kayak or pedalo under the Galetas bridge into the gorge.
around:Gorges du Verdon & Lac de Sainte-.why: Take a canoe, kayak or electric boat a little way up the gorge from the lake; it is the canyon seen from the bottom without the hike.
facts: About 1h45 to 2h by car north from the coast; a full day
A full day: the lake in the morning, then a viewpoint or the Route des Crêtes loop (about 23 km from La Palud-sur-Verdon, closed late November to late March)

The paddle into the gorge from the Galetas bridge. Boat hire is seasonal and many outfits close in autumn, so check; go early on a weekday. The canyon-floor hike is its own card, the Sentier Blanc-Martel
Pair it with Moustiers-Sainte-Marie, at the lake's northern end

around:Moustiers-Sainte-Marie.name: Moustiers-Sainte-Marie
around:Moustiers-Sainte-Marie.teaser: A gilded star hangs on a chain across a cliff gap above a village that has fired faïence since the 1600s
around:Moustiers-Sainte-Marie.story: Moustiers is wedged into a split in the cliff just over the Var's northern line, and high in that split a gilded star hangs on a chain strung from one rock face to the other. The commune tells the oldest version of its origin. The knight Blacas, captured on crusade, vowed to hang a star for the Virgin if he got home, and the star copies his family's arms. Frédéric Mistral wrote the story down in 1885. A second version, about two lovers from feuding families, is told too. Neither can be proved. Below, the village has made tin-glazed faïence since the 17th century, and workshops still fire it.
around:Moustiers-Sainte-Marie.why: Climb the stepped path to the chapel of Notre-Dame de Beauvoir to stand right under the star, then buy a plate from a working atelier rather than a shop.
facts: About 2 hours by car north of the coast, at the northern end of the Lac de Sainte-Croix (Alpes-de-Haute-Provence)
Half a day, best joined to the Verdon
The star and the chapel climb; the Musée de la Faïence, EUR 5, reduced EUR 3, closed Tuesdays (Oct 2026; check the hours)

around:Porquerolles & Port-Cros.name: Porquerolles & Port-Cros
around:Porquerolles & Port-Cros.teaser: A 20-minute crossing to cars-free islands: bikes and white sand on one, steep pine trails on the other
around:Porquerolles & Port-Cros.story: Off Hyères, the two islands you can visit work very differently. Porquerolles is flat enough to cycle, with white-sand coves, vineyards and a contemporary art foundation in the pines. Port-Cros is hilly, green and almost wholly wild. On 14 December 1963 it became the first marine national park in Europe, and its trails climb through holm oak and arbutus to cliffs over clear water. Neither island lets visitors bring a car. Boats run all year, so October, after the summer crowds, is a good month to go. The foundation, the white beach and the snorkel trail each have their own cards.
around:Porquerolles & Port-Cros.why: Hire a bike at the Porquerolles harbour as you land; the far beaches and the vineyards are too far to walk in a day trip.
facts: TLV boats from La Tour Fondue on the Giens peninsula to Porquerolles, daily all year: EUR 22 return in April and October, EUR 17.70 November to March, bike EUR 17 return (Oct 2026). Port-Cros boats leave from Hyères port. The summer bus 67 to La Tour Fondue stopped on 27 September
A full day for one island; do not try both in one go

around:Cotignac.name: Cotignac
around:Cotignac.teaser: A wine village under a 400-metre wall of tufa, its caves once lived in, its two watchtowers still up top
around:Cotignac.story: Cotignac lies at the foot of a wall of tufa 400 metres long and 80 metres high, which the villagers simply call le rocher. The rock is soft enough to carve, so people cut houses, stores and refuges into it. You can climb a path through the old cave dwellings to two so-called Saracen watchtowers and a viewing table over the tiled roofs. Below the rock, plane trees shade the squares and vineyards ring the village. Cotignac joined the Plus Beaux Villages de France in 2022, but it is still a working wine village, not a set for visitors.
around:Cotignac.why: Come on a Tuesday: the morning market fills the village, and the troglodyte site is open that day too.
facts: About 1h10 by car north from the coast
Half a day; pair it with Tourtour and Aups

around:Tourtour & Aups.name: Tourtour & Aups
around:Tourtour & Aups.teaser: A stone village at 635 metres with Sainte-Victoire on the skyline, and the truffle town ten kilometres away
around:Tourtour & Aups.story: Tourtour sits on a ridge at about 635 metres, high enough that the French call it the village dans le ciel, the village in the sky. It is one of the Plus Beaux Villages de France. From its edge on a clear day you see the Maures, the Sainte-Baume and the Montagne Sainte-Victoire, and sometimes as far as Mont Ventoux. About ten kilometres west on the D77 is Aups, a quiet stone town for most of the year that wakes up in winter as the market town of the Haut-Var's black truffle. The two villages make one drive: Tourtour for the view, Aups for the reason to come in winter.
around:Tourtour & Aups.why: Time it for a winter Thursday, when Aups holds its truffle market; out of season, go for the Tourtour view at the end of the day.
facts: About 1h15 to 1h30 by car north from the coast; Aups is about 10 km from Tourtour
Half a day, or a full day with Cotignac
The Tourtour viewpoints in clear weather; the Aups truffle market in season (its own card)

around:Bandol wine country.name: Bandol wine country
around:Bandol wine country.teaser: Terraced vines between two hilltop villages, all turned to the sea, where Bandol's slow red grape ripens
around:Bandol wine country.story: Behind the port of Bandol the land rises in an amphitheatre of stone terraces, the restanques, between the hilltop villages of La Cadière-d'Azur and Le Castellet. They face south to the sea and trap the sun. That matters because the appellation's red is built on mourvèdre, a grape that ripens late and needs the heat to give its dark, savoury fruit. The best estates are tucked among these slopes: Domaine Tempier at Le Plan-du-Castellet, which did most to make Bandol a wine to age; Château de Pibarnon on its high bowl above La Cadière. Walk up into either village and you can see the whole slope at once.
around:Bandol wine country.why: Book one cellar-door tasting ahead, then walk the lanes of Le Castellet; the drink cards cover what to order.
facts: About 35 to 45 minutes by car west of Toulon
A half day for one tasting and one village; a full day with lunch

Domaine Tempier (tastings by appointment; call ahead) and Château de Pibarnon (its own card); the Maison des Vins de Bandol (its own card) to taste across estates; the Fête des Vins de Bandol on the port, 5-6 December 2026
